features.optics-qsfp28: Two 100G QSFP28 ports, 53-54, sold as stacking ports - "subject to NOS implementation, also can be used as data transmission ports". Whether stacking is available is a software question the hardware cannot answer, which is why it is here and not in a group's role.
features.optics-sfp28: Four 10G/25G SFP28 uplinks, ports 49-52. The datasheet's transceiver list gives 10GBASE-RJ-45, 10G DAC/AOC, 25GBASE-SR/LR, 25G DAC/AOC, 40GBASE-SR4/LR4, 40G DAC/AOC, 100GBASE-SR4/CWDM4/LR4 and 100G DAC/AOC for the chassis as a whole; no per-cage breakout table is published, so none is stated here.
features.poe: All forty-eight RJ-45 ports deliver up to 90 W. The key-features list gives the standards per rate group: 36 x 1G/2.5G at IEEE 802.3af/at and bt Type 3/Type 4 90 W, and 12 x 1G/2.5G/5G/10G at the same. Cat 6 cabling, per the datasheet's prose.

WHICH SPELLING THE METAL CARRIES. The datasheet's front elevation prints `AS4630-54NPE` and the quick start guide's port enlargement prints `AS4630-54NPEM`, both legible at 10x, and the two are renders of the same face by the same vendor. The datasheet's body, its title block and all seven of its ordering codes use the shorter form, so that is what is drawn - but a trailing M on a silkscreen is exactly the kind of thing an ordering code drops. A photograph of a real unit's right-hand end closes it.

A SQUARE-ON ELEVATION OF THE EPS201 AND THE EPS202. Neither model's own datasheet figure is orthographic: fitting their twenty-four RJ-45 columns gives rms 0.674 and 0.675 mm against this model's 0.121, with quadratic terms implying the local pitch changes -5.0% and +3.8% across the row. Their quick start guides contain no square-on figure at all. This device's face is measurable and theirs are not, which is why it is modelled first; the EPS201 shares this exact shell and could be carried from here, but the EPS202 is 32 mm shallower and 0.3 mm lower and cannot be assumed to share it.

WHERE EACH PORT'S INDICATOR SITS RELATIVE TO ITS COLUMN. The row is measured - y 38.75 to 40.34, one window per port, number to its left - but at 2.29 px/mm the elevation resolves the band into 78 undifferentiated marks across 48 ports, and the guide's enlargement of that end is calibrated too loosely in x to place them. They are drawn at a quarter-pitch either side of each column centre because that is where the EPS112's are, measured at 11.9 px/mm. One enlargement of this device's lower edge closes it.

A REAR ELEVATION WITHOUT THE 2 PERCENT GRADIENT. The three fan-tray handles - the sharpest repeated feature on the face - measure 38.18, 37.74 and 37.30 wide left to right, and the figure's aspect reads -2.66% where the front's reads +0.66%. Nothing on the rear is wrong by more than about a millimetre, and nothing on it is better than that either. The fan and supply pitches are the reliable figures; their individual widths are not.

finish-and-airflow.note: COUNTED, AND ON THIS FAMILY THE COLOUR IS A CLAIM ABOUT AIRFLOW. Over the whole rear elevation 2,748 pixels pass a red test (R>110, R>G+40, R>B+40) at a median of (239, 57, 39), and every one of them is on the three fan-tray handles; the chassis, the blank plate, the ground point and the two supplies carry none. THE PROSE CONFIRMS IT INDEPENDENTLY, which is what keeps this from being the AIS800 convention imported on faith. This model's datasheet reads "Front-to-back airflow only" and all seven of its ordering codes are -F. Its shell-mate the EPS201 ships both - eight codes, four -F and four -B, and two fan part numbers - and its datasheet's rear draws the handles BLUE while its own guide's fan-replacement figure draws them RED. Red is front-to-back, blue is back-to-front, and this machine only comes one way.

gate-1.note: THIS IS THE ONLY EPS20x FIGURE THAT IS DRAWN STRAIGHT, and finding that out is what decided which of the three to model first. NONE OF THE THREE QUICK START GUIDES CONTAINS A SQUARE-ON ELEVATION - their Overview figures are three-quarter renders with the lid visible - so the only candidates for absolute geometry are the datasheets' Interfaces pages, embedded at about 1000 px across a 438 mm face. That is 2.29 px/mm, one pixel to 0.44 mm, and less than half the instrument the EPS112 had. SO EACH CANDIDATE WAS TESTED FOR ORTHOGRAPHY RATHER THAN JUST FOR ASPECT. Fitting the twenty-four RJ-45 column positions with `first + pitch*i + gutter*(i//6)`, over every row and four thresholds in each figure: this one's best fit has an **rms of 0.121 mm** and adding a quadratic term in i buys nothing (it implies a local-pitch change of -0.7% across the row, which is noise at this scale). The EPS201's best fit over 114 candidate rows is **rms 0.674 mm** and its quadratic implies **-5.0%**; the EPS202's is **rms 0.675 mm** at **+3.8%**. Those two figures are photographed at an angle, and a linear fit on them returns a pitch that is simply wrong - 13.65 mm on the EPS201 against this figure's 14.07 for the same jack. THE ASPECT AGREES with the published dimensions once the figure is known to be straight: the body reads 1002 x 100 px, ratio 10.020 against 438/44 = 9.955, which is +0.66% - within the one pixel that a 100-px-tall figure can resolve. Every measurement in this file uses 2.2877 px/mm with the panel origin at (1, 2). THE CROSS-CHECK THAT MATTERS: the fitted pitch of 14.0706 agrees with the EPS112's 14.0198 and the EPS121's 14.0158 - two other Edgecore access switches, measured on different documents at different scales - to five hundredths of a millimetre. That is the same RJ-45 jack, and it is an independent confirmation that this figure's scale is right.

ground-pair.note: TWO HOLES ON ONE PLATE, ONE ABOVE THE OTHER, AND ONE EARTH SYMBOL TO THEIR RIGHT (#830). The grounding point (datasheet callout 11) is a plate at the far left of the rear with two holes, one above the other. Read on the datasheet rear (fig-0010, body x 131 to 1568 px for 438 and y 516 to 660 px for 44, 3.28 and 3.27 px/mm) the holes centre at x 159 to 161 px and y 554.0 and 607.5 px: x 8.8, y 11.6 and 28.0, 16.4 apart. On the rear photograph (photos 4-EPS203-B, 489 x 357, 1.11 px/mm) at x 12 px and y 166.5 and 184.5 px: x 9.9, y 11.9 and 27.7, 15.8 to 16.2 apart. Drawn at x 9.3, y 11.7 and 27.9, 16.2 apart. The two screws are both common/ground-screw@1, the nominal unsized screw without an earth symbol, and the symbol the chassis prints is silkscreen where it prints it. THE SYMBOL is a circled IEC earth printed to the RIGHT of the holes, midway between them: its ring centres at (196.1, 581.9) px on the datasheet rear, (19.9, 20.1), and at about (24, 175) px on the photograph, (20.7, 19.7), about 11.7 across on both. Drawn at (20.2, 20.1), ring radius 5.6. NO SIZE IS CLAIMED: neither document names the screw or a lug, so no pair host is placed. Formerly one common/ground-lug@1, ground, whose stud sat between the holes and to their right, at (15.5, 24.8).

power.note: THE SUPPLY IS 1200 W AND THE DRAWING SAYS OTHERWISE. Three published statements agree: the Power section's "2pcs 1+1 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable 1200 W AC (80 PLUS Platinum compliant)", the Interfaces callouts "9. PSU 2: 1200 Watts" and "10. PSU 1: 1200 Watts", and the ordering table's "YPEB1200AM-1A03P10 ... 1200 W AC Power Supply (3Y)". The rear elevation prints "2kV 920W" on each supply's fan hub, legible at 12x, and three published statements outrank one silkscreen on a render, so 1200 is carried and the hub text is recorded. WHAT THE HUB TEXT IS was worked out afterwards, on `edgecore/eps202`, and this note is corrected rather than left as it was. That machine takes the SAME supply - the ordering table names both chassis - and its rear elevation prints "2kV 1200W" on the same hub. So the label tracks the supply's output, not the fan, and this figure's "920W" is an inconsistency between two renders of one part rather than a different quantity. The conclusion here was right; the first explanation of it was not. THE MACHINE'S FIGURES: maximum power consumption "Low-line: 2000 Watts High-line: 2400 Watts"; input "Low-line: 15A for 90VAC-136VAC (1000 Watts) High-line: 8.A for 180VAC -264VAC (1200 Watts)", the high-line current printed with a missing digit in the source; PoE budget with a 30 W guard band "Low-line: 700 W for 1 PSU/1700 W for 2 PSU, High-line: 900 W for 1 PSU/2100 W for 2 PSU".

sources.note: EACH OF THE THREE EPS20x MODELS HAS ITS OWN GUIDE AND ITS OWN DATASHEET - six distinct files, no two sharing a hash, unlike the EPS121/EPS122 pair. This model's are eps203-qsg.pdf (md5 5d12d3c155d2c7f797d9dc9d1dfee0df) and eps203-datasheet.pdf (md5 2de53f6bea0e8050273532607423eaf0). THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE ABOUT THE MODEL NAME PRINTED ON THE PANEL. The datasheet's front elevation prints `AS4630-54NPE`, legible at 10x; the guide's port enlargement prints `AS4630-54NPEM`. The datasheet's body uses the shorter spelling nineteen times including its title block and every one of its seven ordering codes; the guide uses each spelling six times. The shorter one is drawn here because it is what this device's own elevation carries and what the ordering codes buy, and the disagreement is recorded as a gap rather than resolved by preference.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 2 SFP pairs (port-49/port-50 and port-51/port-52), the 1 QSFP pair (port-53/port-54).

the-port-indicators.note: ONE INDICATOR PER PORT in a row below the port wall, with the port's number printed to its left - the datasheet's callout 6 on the EPS201's identical face calls them "Port indicators", and the guide's legend gives the vocabulary: "RJ-45 Port LEDs: Green (link), Blinking (activity)", "SFP28 Port LEDs: White (25G), Green (10G), Blinking (activity)", "QSFP28 Port LEDs: White (100G), Green (40G link), Blinking (activity)". THE ROW IS MEASURED AND THE PER-PORT OFFSETS ARE DERIVED, and the difference is worth stating. The band reads y 38.75 to 40.34 on the guide's enlargement, where y is anchored on the bezel plate and does not depend on that crop's x scale; the count is one per port, legible. THE INDIVIDUAL OFFSETS ARE NOT MEASURABLE HERE: on the elevation at 2.29 px/mm a 2 mm window and a 3 mm digit are four and six pixels and the band resolves into 78 undifferentiated marks across 48 ports. So each port's indicator is placed at a quarter-pitch either side of its column centre - 3.518 mm - which is where the EPS112's are, measured at 11.9 px/mm on the same vendor's same legend style. Derived from a measurement of a sibling, not measured here, and said so.

the-port-wall.note: FORTY-EIGHT RJ-45 IN TWENTY-FOUR COLUMNS OF TWO, ganged six and six and six and six. Fitted over all twenty-four columns on the bright dividers between ports: **pitch 14.0706, gutter 4.1518, first centre 34.5102, rms 0.121 mm, max residual 0.215**. The residuals show no bow, which is the test the other two figures fail. THE ROWS MIRROR, and which row is rotated was measured rather than assumed. On the guide's left-end enlargement the upper row's wide body occupies its cell from +3.45 to +10.36 mm, where `std/rj45-ganged@2` rotated 180 puts it at +3.67 to +10.5 and unrotated would put it at +0.5 to +7.33; the lower row's reads +0.95 to +7.85, which is the unrotated case. So `rotate: {top: 180}`, the same way round as the EPS112. THE ROW PITCH IS 13.92 AND COMES FROM THE BEZEL PLATE, not from the aperture centres, for the reason the EPS112 records: mirrored rows are not symmetric about their cells. The plate reads y 11.802 to 36.719 at two independent columns - height 24.916 - and two 11.0 mm cells fill it with 2.92 between them. The EPS112's plate is 25.015 and its row pitch 13.94, measured on a different document; the two agree to a tenth of a millimetre, which is what one shared jack housing should do. THEN FOUR SFP28 as two stacked pairs at x 388.83 and 403.25 - cage apertures 13.55 wide, rows at 16.61 and 30.82 - and TWO QSFP28 as one stacked pair at x 422.48, its cage 17.92 wide against `std/qsfp-ganged@1`'s 18.5, rows at 16.61 and 31.70.

the-rear.note: MEASURED ON THIS MODEL'S OWN REAR ELEVATION at 2.2785 px/mm - 998 px across 438 mm - and it is the weaker of the two figures: its aspect reads -2.66% against 438 x 44, and the three fan-tray handles measure 38.18, 37.74 and 37.30 wide, a 2% spread in one direction. So the rear carries about a millimetre of slack where the front carries a tenth, and every figure below is stated at that accuracy. THE BAY NUMBERS ARE OBSERVED AND NOT DRAWN. The elevation prints a small fan glyph and a numeral - 1, 2, 3 - on the chassis web beside each tray, at about x 88, 137 and 186. At 2.28 px/mm that web is one millimetre wide, which is two pixels and less than the figure's own gradient, so any placement would either sit on the tray - where a seated module hides it, which is the thing lint's overlap rule exists to catch - or be invented. The marks are recorded here instead of drawn. THREE FAN TRAY BAYS at x 46.1, 94.1 and 142.4 on a pitch of 48.15, each 39.5 wide and running y 2.5 to 42.0. THE WIDTH IS NOT THE PITCH: there is an 8.6 mm chassis web between trays, which a first pass through this figure missed by reading each seam as the end of the tray before it rather than the start of the tray after. The EPS201's rear, measured the same way, gives all six edges - 47.4-86.4, 95.1-134.2, 143.6-182.6 - and the handle settles it, because a 38-to-40 mm bar cannot be bolted to a 47.5 mm tray and leave the seams where they are. A BLANK PLATE from about x 192 to 268 with a single screw. TWO SUPPLY BAYS at x 270.0 and 354.0, 72.0 wide on a pitch of 84.0, and the chassis prints PS2 and PS1 on the web to the right of each. THE GROUNDING POINT is a plate at the far left, x 4 to 44, with two holes one above the other at x 9.3 and an IEC earth symbol in a circle to their right, midway between them at (20.2, 20.1) - the datasheet's callout 11 (provenance ground-pair).

the-status-lamps-and-buttons.note: EIGHT LAMPS IN TWO ROWS OF FOUR, and the datasheet's own list names only seven. The panel reads System / PSU1 / STK1 / FAN across the top and PRI / PSU2 / STK2 / PoE across the bottom, with each label to the right of its lamp; the datasheet's LEDs section lists "PRI, PSU1, PSU2, STK1, STK2, FAN, PoE" and omits System. Eight are drawn because eight is what the panel shows, and the guide's legend names all eight. MEASURED ON THE GUIDE'S BUTTON/LAMP ENLARGEMENT at 10.0422 px/mm - calibrated on four port-column centres this file already knows exactly, with a fit rms of 0.11 px, or 0.011 mm. The lamps are 2.888 x 1.494, on x centres 154.18, 162.05, 170.01 and 177.88 - a pitch of 7.90 - with rows centred y 3.74 and 7.22. TWO ROUND BUTTONS to their left: STK M/S at x 136.61 and Reset at x 145.97, both about 2.2 mm across on y 5.0. The guide legends them "STK M/S button" and "Reset button" and gives the stacking behaviour with the STK1/STK2 lamps. THE LAMP ROWS ARE DRAWN 0.70 mm ABOVE WHERE THE ENLARGEMENT PUTS THEM, and that is a reconciliation rather than a reading. The enlargement's y is anchored on the bezel plate and gives rows at 3.74 and 7.22; the elevation puts the port-numeral band at 7.43 to 8.74, which would have the lower lamp row painting over the numerals for columns nine to eleven. The two crops disagree by about half a millimetre and the elevation is the one whose y is not borrowed, so the lamps move. Both figures are written down here so the next reader can take the other view. THE `Mgmt (up) (down) Console` LEGEND'S x IS NOT MEASURED. It is present and its reading order is unambiguous, but the only crop that shows it is the guide's left-end enlargement, whose x scale could not be tied down: its port openings imply 7.53 px/mm and its indicator spacing implies 6.9, a nine percent disagreement that no anchor in the crop resolves. The four marks are placed symmetrically about the jack pair's measured centre instead.

the-two-copper-rates-are-two-groups.note: THE DATASHEET SPLITS THE COPPER ROW AND THE SPLIT LANDS ON A GANG BOUNDARY. Its Interfaces callouts read "3. 36 x 100M/1000M/2.5G ports" and "4. 12 x 1G/2.5G/5G/10GBASE-T ports", and on the elevation callout 3's bracket covers the first three gangs and callout 4's the fourth. Eighteen columns then six columns; thirty-six ports then twelve. So ports 1-36 and 37-48 are two groups, and unlike the EPS112 - where the PoE split fell in the middle of a gang - here the metal and the grouping agree. BOTH GROUPS CARRY PoE UP TO 90 W. The prose is explicit: "all RJ-45 Ethernet ports can support up to 90 W Power-over-Ethernet" and "up to 90 Watts ... for all 48 RJ-45 ports, including the 10G ports". The key-features list gives the standards per group - 802.3af/at and bt Type 3/Type 4 on both - which is why the rate, not the PoE, is what separates them.

the-vent.note: A HEXAGONAL PERFORATION BAND along the top of the face, y 0.1 to 5.4. Measured on the guide's left-end enlargement at 7.53 px/mm, where eight separate rows of the image agree: **pitch 3.717 mm with a coefficient of variation of 0.009**, holes 2.39 across. The EPS112's are 3.611 and 2.70 - the same perforation tooling at a slightly different pitch. THE BAND'S ENDS ARE THE WEAK FIGURE. On the elevation the band reads dark from about x 26 to the right end with the button and lamp plate interrupting it, and at 2.29 px/mm the segment boundaries are good to about a millimetre. Two rects are drawn, x 26-128 and 192-382, and that is the accuracy claimed.

why-the-parts-are-named-for-their-FRUs.note: THE ORDERING TABLES NAME THE PARTS AND SAY WHICH CHASSIS TAKE THEM. `FAN-1U-1x1M` is listed in all three EPS20x datasheets as "Fan Module ... (for EPS201/AS4630-54TE, EPS202/AS4630-54PE, EPS203/AS4630-54NPE)" - one tray in three chassis - so the part is `edgecore/eps200-fan-tray@1` rather than being named after this one. `YPEB1200AM-1A03P10` is "1200 W AC Power Supply (3Y) ... (for EPS202/AS4630-54PE, EPS203/AS4630-54NPE)" - two chassis, not three, because the EPS201 takes a 150 W `YM-1151D` instead - so it is `edgecore/eps200-psu-1200w@1`. This is the ruling roc-ops/Portrayal#426 made for the 2RU fan tray applied before the second chassis arrives rather than after.
